name: Elafonisi
seoTitle: Elafonisi Pink Sand Beach: Drive Time, Lagoon and Visitor Tips
seoDescription: Elafonisi is the pink sand beach and lagoon at the south-west tip of Crete, about 2.5 hours from Rethymno. Entry is free and you can wade across to the islet.
summary: Elafonisi is a pink-sand beach and shallow lagoon at the far south-western tip of Crete, roughly two and a half hours by road from Rethymno. The pink comes from crushed shells of a red-pigmented organism mixed into the white sand, showing as bands along the waterline that vary with tide and light. A lagoon a few tens of centimetres deep separates the mainland beach from Elafonisi islet, a protected nature reserve you can wade to in a couple of minutes; the sand is pinker on the islet and the crowds thin out immediately. Entry is free, parking is charged, and the drive is long enough that this is a full day rather than an afternoon.
body:
## The pink sand

The colour is real and it is not uniform. Fragments of red foraminifera shells wash up and mix with the white sand, so the pink concentrates where the water has recently been: in strips along the shoreline, in pockets between rocks, and most reliably on the islet side. Bright midday sun washes it out; morning and late afternoon show it best. Taking the sand away is illegal, and the reason the colour has faded in the most trafficked spots.

## The lagoon and the islet

Elafonisi islet lies a short distance offshore, separated by water usually ankle to knee deep. Wading across takes a couple of minutes and is the single best thing to do here. The islet is a protected Natura 2000 site with dunes, sea daffodils, juniper and marked paths, quieter beaches on its far side and a memorial to the 1824 massacre of Cretans who had sheltered there. Loggerhead turtles nest on these beaches, which is why the dunes are fenced.

## Getting there

There is no short way. From Rethymno the drive is around two and a half hours each way, west across the island and then down through the mountains of south-west Chania, on roads that are narrow and slow for the final stretch. Most itineraries break the journey at Topolia Gorge or the Agia Sophia cave above it. Leaving early matters twice over: for the light on the sand, and for a space in the car park.

## Practicalities

Access is free; parking is charged in season. Sunbeds and umbrellas are rented and sell out fast, and there are canteens but no real shade of any kind, so a hat and a towel are worth carrying. Facilities are basic for somewhere this well known. The wind picks up in the afternoon on this coast.

faqs.q: Is the sand at Elafonisi really pink?
faqs.a: Yes, though it is banded rather than uniform. Crushed red shell fragments concentrate along the waterline and in pockets among the rocks, and the colour reads strongest in morning and late-afternoon light.

faqs.q: How long is the drive from Rethymno to Elafonisi?
faqs.a: About two and a half hours each way. That is why it is a full-day trip: roughly five hours of driving around four or so hours at the beach.

faqs.q: Can you walk to Elafonisi island?
faqs.a: Yes. The lagoon between the mainland beach and the islet is normally ankle to knee deep and takes a couple of minutes to cross. The sand is pinker on the far side and it is considerably quieter.
No. The beach is free to enter. You pay for parking, and for a sunbed and umbrella if you want them.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Elafonisi?
faqs.a: May, June, September and early October: warm water, softer light on the sand and far fewer people than July and August, when the car park fills by mid-morning.
